mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital decreases for corporations and investors.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.0% signals economic distress and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings face downward pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) level signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits improve.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during the post-shock recovery regime, or the Rank IC over the recovery period is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 130,000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a declining real interest rate, which stimulates economic activity and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through the interaction of these two monetary indicators.
failure_condition: The joint signal of decreasing FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime, rising retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from increased spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during the early-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over the early-cycle period is less than 0.03.
